prompt.context: You are presented with financial data for three anonymous companies — Company A, Company B, and Company C.
prompt.question: Here is information about Companies A, B, and C. What can you make of this data? And can you determine what type of industry each one is in?

exhibits.title: Financial Data for Companies A, B, and C
exhibits.shows: A table of financial figures for three anonymous companies: Net Income After Taxes, Revenues, Assets, Liabilities, and Equity

framework: Calculate key financial ratios: ROA, ROE, Net Profit Margin, Debt-to-Assets, Debt-to-Equity
Note: Current Ratio cannot be computed because Total (not Current) Assets and Liabilities are given
Interpret each ratio relative to the others to characterize each company's business model
Match ratio profiles to likely industry types: high-margin/low-volume, high-leverage financial, high-volume/low-margin

questions.prompt: Calculate ROA, ROE, Net Profit Margin, Debt-to-Assets, and Debt-to-Equity for each company
questions.guidance: ROA = Net Income / Assets; ROE = Net Income / Equity; Net Profit Margin = Net Income / Revenues; Debt-to-Assets = Liabilities / Assets; Debt-to-Equity = Liabilities / Equity. Use these to profile each company.

math.setup: Apply standard ratio formulas to the exhibit data for each company
steps: Co. A: ROA = 254M/2.8B = 9%; ROE = 254M/1.8B = 14%; Net Profit Margin = 254M/2.6B = 10%; Debt-to-Assets = 1.0B/2.8B = 36%; Debt-to-Equity = 1.0B/1.8B = 56%
Co. B: ROA = 7B/1.121T = 1%; ROE = 7B/35B = 20%; Net Profit Margin = 7B/77B = 9%; Debt-to-Assets = 1.085T/1.121T = 97%; Debt-to-Equity = 1.085T/35B = 3103%
Co. C: ROA = 11B/151B = 7%; ROE = 11B/61B = 18%; Net Profit Margin = 11B/348B = 3%; Debt-to-Assets = 89B/151B = 60%; Debt-to-Equity = 89B/61B = 148%
math.answer: Co. A: ROA 9%, ROE 14%, Margin 10%, D/A 36%, D/E 56%. Co. B: ROA 1%, ROE 20%, Margin 9%, D/A 97%, D/E 3103%. Co. C: ROA 7%, ROE 18%, Margin 3%, D/A 60%, D/E 148%.

questions.prompt: Based on the ratios, what type of industry is each company in?
questions.guidance: Co. A has the highest ROA and Net Profit Margin but the lowest leverage — consistent with a low-volume, high-margin specialty retailer such as a luxury goods or jewelry company (actual: Tiffany & Co.). Co. B has extremely high Debt-to-Equity (3103%) and near-equal assets and liabilities — classic hallmarks of a leveraged financial institution such as a bank or investment bank (actual: Morgan Stanley). Co. C has the lowest Net Profit Margin (3%) and very high revenues relative to net income — consistent with a high-volume, low-margin mass retailer (actual: Wal-Mart).

recommendation: Co. A is a low-volume, high-margin company — likely a luxury or specialty retailer (Tiffany & Co.)
Co. B is a highly leveraged financial institution with near-parity between assets and liabilities (Morgan Stanley)
Co. C is a high-volume, low-margin mass retailer (Wal-Mart)
risks: Ratio analysis alone cannot pinpoint the exact company; multiple firms could fit each profile
Extreme leverage at Co. B highlights significant financial risk if assets lose value
Low margins at Co. C mean profitability is sensitive to cost increases or revenue shortfalls
next_steps: Request additional data (current assets/liabilities) to compute liquidity ratios such as the Current Ratio
Compare ratios against industry benchmarks to validate the industry identification
Examine revenue and asset trends over time to assess sustainability of each business model
